verdict.rationale: The MCP plugin explicitly lets your app act as an OAuth authorization server and protected resource, though only for Model Context Protocol clients. The Device Authorization plugin implements the RFC 8628 code issuance and approval flow, and the JWT plugin exposes token and JWKS endpoints, so the building blocks for issuing tokens exist. No evidence shows a general-purpose OAuth/OIDC provider for arbitrary third-party clients; the SSO plugin is consumer-side. Missing for 10: a documented general OAuth2/OIDC provider for arbitrary third-party apps, client registration and management, consent screens, standard authorization-code flow docs, and independent hands-on corroboration.
